It's honestly the best indicator I have yet to discover, since I often don't really notice when I shift moods.

I'm craving (in person) social interaction, and I am having a really hard time getting it to happen. I even had plans with someone today, but it's looking like they're going to bail.

How're things going for all of you guys? I feel like I should post here more when I am not depressed to even out the tone. Back when I participated in the community on Reddit I noticed it started turning into mostly people talking about how they were down, and getting the generic "hang in there" kind of responses. Something I think we all know, given the cyclic nature of bipolar. Maybe I'm just more interested in meaningful discussion and learning about other people while talking about myself.
After two weeks of hypomania I woke up feeling lonely and unwanted.

I'm trying to wait this depression out and "hang in there" the best I can. Those thoughts of wanting to die keep coming and going, and I have no energy or motivation at work. I honestly should probably be off work, but I can't afford it. Tomorrow I pick up a script for Prozac because the Wellbutrin is not working.

I, for one, appreciate your feedback and posts. I feel like I am being held hostage by my own mind, and no one around me really understands.

I remember when I was working while depressed. Looking back I really do not know how I managed every day. I always despise how I can't help acting like nothing is wrong. On my break I would beg my mind to let me cry. Hiding the depression was just the natural reaction to it. Sometimes I just wanted someone to say anything - no matter how meaningless. I feel like I tried very hard to make it obvious, but I don't think it ever was. There was too much of me that was too proud to expose my true state of mind, I guess.

This was the case sometimes even with my therapist. I would go in miserable, then through talking everything would seem alright. Then I would leave and realize how everything was just a facade. All the energy and hopes and plans and confidence would be left in the room and I would return to the hopeless misery. Sometimes I wrote things down, but they always seemed so dumb later on.

I never had much luck with anti-depressants. Other than my primary medication (lamotrigine) the only thing that's really helped has been reducing stress, which mostly precludes a job. I'm at a reasonably stable place right now, and I really want to work again, but in many ways it's frightening. I don't want to be back to where I got to.
